explication:
<explanation>
1. Project Type & Purpose  
   - This is a Node.js–based CLI tool and local MCP (Model-Context-Protocol) server (“chrome-devtools-mcp”) that lets AI coding assistants control and inspect a live Chrome instance via DevTools.  
   - It exposes a set of “tools” (click, navigate, performance trace, etc.) over MCP, dispatches incoming tool calls to Puppeteer/DevTools, and returns structured MCP responses.

2. File Structure → Architectural Components  
   - src/cli.ts, src/main.ts, src/index.ts  
     • Entry points: parse CLI args, initialize MCP server (via modelcontextprotocol-sdk), wire in tools, start listening on stdio or pipes.  
   - src/browser.ts, src/polyfill.ts, src/Mutex.ts, src/WaitForHelper.ts, src/PageCollector.ts  
     • Core browser-control layer: launches or connects to Chrome (puppeteer under the hood), manages concurrency, waits for events, collects pages.  
   - src/tools/*.ts  
     • Individual tool implementations: each exports a definition (name, params) and handler that uses browser layer to perform actions.  
   - src/formatters/*.ts  
     • Post-processing layer: take raw DevTools data (network events, snapshots) and turn it into human-readable or MCP response objects.  
   - src/trace-processing/parse.ts  
     • Parser for Chrome trace files, exposing structured performance insights.  
   - src/utils/*.ts  
     • Shared helpers (pagination, type definitions) used throughout.  
   - src/third_party/modelcontextprotocol-sdk  
     • MCP protocol library: defines request/response wire format, server starter, tool registration API.  
   - Configuration & Build  
     • rollup.config.mjs, tsconfig.json, eslint.config.mjs, scripts/prepare.ts → your build pipeline (TypeScript → bundled JS CLI).  
   - Tests & Docs  
     • tests/ → unit tests for each module (not part of runtime diagram).  
     • docs/ → Markdown references (outside scope of runtime architecture).

3. Main Components & Relationships  
   Draw these core runtime boxes and their interactions:  
   A. CLI Process  
     • Parses args & flags → invokes MCPServer bootstrap.  
   B. MCPServer (modelcontextprotocol-sdk)  
     • Registers all tools from src/tools → listens for incoming MCP tool calls (stdin/stdout).  
   C. Tool Registry & Dispatcher  
     • On request: find matching tool handler, invoke it with args.  
   D. Browser Controller  
     • launch/connect Chrome via Puppeteer, maintain session, multiplex pages (PageCollector).  
   E. DevTools Protocol Client  
     • Under Puppeteer’s hood or direct CDP calls used by tools and formatters.  
   F. Tool Handlers  
     • Use Browser Controller & DevTools Protocol to perform actions (click, navigate, trace).  
   G. Formatters & Trace Processor  
     • Take raw data or trace file → transform into structured JSON/MCP responses.  
   H. MCP Response → back to client  

   External: Chrome browser process (blue box)  
   Internal libraries: third_party MCP SDK (orange), utils/helpers (orange)  
   Build & Test: greyed out, left side or bottom of diagram

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Modular tool-based design (one handler per tool) → easily extensible.  
   - Separation of concerns: CLI bootstrap vs. MCP server core vs. browser layer vs. formatters vs. trace parsing.  
   - Single responsibility: each src/*.ts has a clear role.  
   - Uses a protocol abstraction (modelcontextprotocol-sdk) to decouple transport (stdin/stdout) from tool logic.

5. Tailoring Diagram to an “Open-Source Tool”  
   - Emphasize core functionality: tool registry, browser control, DevTools integration.  
   - Highlight extension points: src/tools folder (where new tools plug in), third_party SDK.  
   - Show external dependency: Puppeteer & Chrome.

6. Diagram Guidelines for the Principal Engineer  
   - Components: use distinct shapes/colors:  
     • Green rectangles for runtime modules (CLI, MCPServer, Tool Handlers, Browser Controller, Formatters)  
     • Blue cylinder or process icon for Chrome browser  
     • Orange boxes for third-party or shared libraries (modelcontextprotocol-sdk, utils)  
   - Connect with directional arrows showing data flow:  
     • Client → CLI → MCPServer → Tool Dispatcher → Browser Controller → Chrome  
     • Chrome → DevTools events → Tool Handler → Formatter → MCPServer → Client  
   - Label each arrow with the type of message (e.g., “MCP Request: performance_start_trace”, “CDP Command”, “Trace Data”).  
   - Include a legend explaining colors/shapes.  
   - Optionally annotate sequence order for a typical tool call.

7. Detail Level & Best Practices  
   - Do not group everything as “src”: break it into logical runtime subsystems.  
   - Keep testing/build artifacts off the core diagram—perhaps annotate them as “CI/CD” on the side.  
   - Include configuration loader (CLI args) if space allows, since it drives headless vs. headful, wsEndpoint, etc.  
   - Capture the user-data-dir concept (persistent profile vs. isolated) as a note near Browser Controller.  
   - Review after drafting: ensure every src sub-folder appears in one of the runtime boxes.

By following this mapping from file tree & README to runtime components, you’ll produce a clear, accurate, and detailed system design diagram for `chrome-devtools-mcp`.  
</explanation>
